item.title: Tuesday, November 24, 2026
item.description:
Analysis agents, scored blind

Novák et al. arXiv:2611.28194 give the AI-agent thread its first scorecard for experimental analysis. Each agent builds a single workflow on CMS open data, and that workflow is then run on sealed datasets with injected signals and shifted detector settings. Averaged over four tasks, Gemini 4 Argon reaches 60% of the expert reference score, GPT 6 Astra 38% and Claude Opus 5.5 31%. The last is the same model that delivered verified Feynman-integral bases yesterday. Theory output can be checked exactly; analysis output has to be checked by injection, and this is the first benchmark to do that, putting into practice Alimena’s evidence-over-code standard from 11-19. Also today: three trigger papers working at tens to hundreds of nanoseconds, a list of DM assumptions that matter more than expected, and colour that refuses to stay subleading.

Themes

Triggers in nanoseconds

This is new; nothing in recent memory covers it. - Learned event embedding. Rozanov et al. arXiv:2611.28355 distill an offline transformer into a 7512-parameter quantised Level-1 encoder running in 147 ns. It rejects 99% of background while keeping 96% of held-out SM processes and 88% of 52 BSM benchmarks. - Symbolic anomaly detector. Bollhalder et al. arXiv:2611.30896 distill a normalising-flow anomaly detector into an explicit 577-operation formula that runs in 42.8 ns. - CMS Phase-2 muons. Estrada et al. arXiv:2611.30394 detect muon showers from Drift Tube hits in about 20 ns.

Signature-agnostic selection now fits inside the L1 latency budget.

Dark matter’s quieter assumptions

  • Halo shape. Shao et al. arXiv:2611.29197 find that halo anisotropy moves LZ elastic limits by ±30% above 40 GeV but by up to 10× below 15 GeV.
  • Resonant freeze-out. Arcadi et al. arXiv:2611.28230 drop the kinetic-equilibrium assumption at the Higgs resonance. The coupling needed for the relic abundance shifts by up to 10× for pseudoscalar fermion DM, which strengthens direct-detection constraints.
  • Single-electron backgrounds. Santos-Olmsted et al. arXiv:2611.28211 propose using xenon detectors’ full dark-electron rate in an annual-modulation search. Sensitivity then scales as S≲√(B) rather than S≲B, with no new hardware.

This continues the week’s habit of auditing error bars, now applied to dark matter.

Plumbing for EFT fits

  • SMEFT plus PDFs. Cole et al. arXiv:2611.28216 fit 15 Wilson coefficients and the proton PDFs simultaneously. They add parity violation via LEFT matching and include charged-current high-mass Drell–Yan for the first time. The PDFs barely move.
  • EFT-safe acceptance. ATLAS arXiv:2611.30272 recasts H→4ℓ STXS into a Lorentz-invariant fiducial region with A^LIF_SM=0.8546, production-independent to 0.07%. EFT reinterpretations then need no EFT-dependent efficiency corrections.

EFT is the year’s standard collider language, and these papers are infrastructure for it.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.28194 (Novák et al.): The model rankings will date fast. The sealed-world design, with injection tests applied to a single fixed workflow, is the lasting contribution.
  • arXiv:2611.29072 (Chargeishvili): Exact full-colour soft evolution up to 15 gluons, an 8×10⁸-dimensional colour space handled on one node. For gap-vetoed jet rates, leading colour overestimates the full result by 1.3×, 1.8× and 6.6× at 8, 10 and 14 partons.
  • arXiv:2611.29197 (Shao et al.): For the 248 keV LZ event, some anisotropic halos make splittings kinematically accessible where solar-neutrino bounds on the higgsino lose force. That is the constraint that has excluded the higgsino reading since Pospelov. The authors stress that kinematic access does not establish viability.
  • arXiv:2611.29717 (Chen et al.): Magic production vanishes for single gluon, photon, W, Higgs and graviton exchange, and for leptonic Z exchange at sin²θ_W=1/4. The result is computed in the chirality basis, so the basis-dependence of magic measures reported by Altomonte et al. on 11-16 applies here too.
  • arXiv:2611.30877 (Reboud et al.): Subtract one simple pole per narrow resonance, then convolve the smooth remainder on a grid set by the detector resolution. This is a structural answer to the normalisation problems from sharply localized terms that Zhu et al. flagged on 11-17.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.31214 Massive de Sitter correlators at one loop — Amara McCune (hep-th). Exact squeezed signals from heavy SM loops come out 10–30× larger than late-time estimates. This is the week’s third exact cosmological-correlator result.
  • arXiv:2611.29939 Ionization of gravitational atoms by a companion-sourced Yukawa potential — Yi Wang et al. (gr-qc). A Yukawa force sourced by the companion can halt superradiant growth, extending the binary-environment effect on superradiance clouds noted on 11-20.
  • arXiv:2611.28208 Bring Your Own Instanton… — Csaba Csáki et al. (hep-th). Rubakov–Callan catalysis proceeds via sourced instantons without exponential suppression. It is an IR effect: the scattering fermions never reach the monopole core.
  • arXiv:2611.31080 Kaon-pair production with NNLO effects — Yizhou Fang et al. (hep-ph). McMule now covers e⁺e⁻→KK̅ at NNLO in initial-state QED, with very large corrections at CMD-3 energies. Relevant to HVP and the radiative-return generator comparison from 11-23.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.28194 — HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds (Andrzej Novák et al.)

Each agent gets one session of at most 7.5 h on a public world built from 2016 CMS open simulation (MiniAOD, full detector simulation). It must deliver a single pipeline, which is then frozen and rerun on 10–40 sealed worlds per task. Every world has a hidden truth (m_H, μ, Γ_H/Γ_H^SM, or lepton and jet corrections) and one of 13 detector profiles that distort scale, resolution and efficiencies. The score is a strictly proper log score relative to an expert reference run on the same worlds. A shared-bias term growing like √(N) is added, along with weighted reviewer checks: goodness of fit, truthfulness against an evaluator refit, and Z-peak closure. With γ=2, the ratio reads as an effective fraction of the data.

Across 99 sessions per task and eleven models: - Gemini 4 Argon averages 60±8% of the reference, GPT 6 Astra 38%, Claude Opus 5.5 31%. - No open-weight model exceeds 10%. - Sessions undercover far more often than they overcover. - Run-to-run spread exceeds the differences between prompt tiers. Opus 5.5 on HiggsLepMass reaches 89% in its best session against a 49% mean. - The P2 expert plan adds nothing over P1.

The harness is validated adversarially. A memorised 125 GeV scores <1% and understated uncertainties score 34%. With ten worlds, every flawed archetype falls below the reference in ≥96% of draws.

Caveats the authors flag: - Worlds vary detector response and signal, but not generators. The six JetCalib sessions that beat the reference gain mainly because the reference’s modelling-dominated JES uncertainties exceed the injected variations. - Scores depend on the chosen reference and weights. - Only one experiment is covered.

arXiv:2611.29072 — A billion colour states: exact soft-gluon evolution beyond leading colour for many-jet QCD (Bakar Chargeishvili)

Leading colour degrades steadily with multiplicity. Take a soft veto outside the jets at t=0.1 (Q/Q_0≈14), inside the t≈0.05–0.12 range the author maps to LHC dijet vetoes. There, LC overestimates the full-colour no-emission factor by median factors of 1.27, 1.83 and 6.6 at 8, 10 and 14 partons. The gap fraction is off by 2.2 at n=14. Pairs among the three hardest jets form a colour singlet 3–9% of the time; LC sets this to zero.

The method builds an orthogonal multiplet basis by coupling partons one leg at a time, with each step fixed by a Casimir eigenvalue (Jucys–Murphy elements). Norms come in closed form, and dipoles act only on the label segment between the two partons, via small recoupling tables. Γ is therefore never stored: Γx is a block “sweep” and e⁻tΓ a Krylov iteration. Fourteen gluons take about an hour on one A100. Fifteen gluons (827,888,726 states) take 3–7 h per t value on a CPU node with up to 857 GB.

For showers, the formal 1/N_c² suppression is outweighed by the growing number of unconnected pairs. Caveats: - The calculation uses one-loop Γ at fixed coupling, with colour-diagonal factors dropped. - Events are flat in phase space, and real emission is included only up to five hard partons. - Independent cross-checks stop at n≤7. Beyond that, validation rests on internal consistency. - The n=15 points show feasibility and do not enter the LC comparison.

arXiv:2611.29197 — Quantifying the Impact of Galactic Dark Matter Halo Models on LZ Results (Jialiang Shao et al.)

The authors rescale LZ limits by the ratio of predicted yields across 22 self-consistent BCFS halos, truncated at a common v_esc=544 km/s.

Elastic results: - Above about 40 GeV, the SI envelope is R≈0.8–1.3 relative to the SHM. - At 9 GeV it opens to 0.17–1.63 (class B). - Extending the class-D cutoff to 1000 km/s drives R to about 0.04. - At 9 GeV, the v_esc scan (factor ~2 for classes A/B) and the efficiency treatment (factor 2–3) matter about as much as the halo. - In the SD channel at 40 GeV, nuclear-structure uncertainty (factors 3.6 and 13 for neutron and proton) still exceeds the roughly 2× halo spread.

For the 248 keV event (LZ: 3.4σ local, 2.6σ global), they use a background-free single-event likelihood at 1.1 TeV. The tail sets the inelastic ceiling: δ_max≈384 keV for the SHM and 556 keV for an LMC-like tail. The higgsino cross section (~7×10⁻³⁹ cm²) crosses these two contours at δ≈360 and 455 keV, both below the 566 keV solar-neutrino threshold. Some anisotropic contours reach 700–775 keV, but only at cross sections well below the higgsino value (D1/D3 near 3×10⁻⁴⁰ cm²).

Caveats: - Limits are rescaled by yield ratio rather than refit with the LZ likelihood. - The suite is not a posterior, and it mixes profile, rotation and anisotropy. - The 1000 km/s cutoffs are sensitivity tests, not measurements. - The single-event fit assumes unit efficiency, and its coverage is uncalibrated.

Full text for arXiv:2611.29717 (Chen et al.) and arXiv:2611.30877 (Reboud et al.) was not supplied, so those picks are not expanded here.

item.title: Monday, November 23, 2026
item.description:
Toponium and a pseudoscalar must interfere

The year’s longest interpretive fight asks whether the tt̅ threshold excess is NRQCD η_t or a top-philic CP-odd Higgs. Djouadi et al. arXiv:2611.27704 show the two readings cannot be fitted separately. An A near 2m_t sits in the same colour-singlet ¹S_0 channel with the same Coulomb interaction, so the two must interfere. Unitarity then fixes the line shape through a single complex ratio κ, with an exact amplitude zero just above M_A. Fits that simply add toponium and A templates are therefore wrong by construction. Also today: an LLM agent delivering new Feynman-integral bases, a 6.3σ strike against the Körner–Pati–Woo rule, and the first NNLO+PS generator for e⁺e⁻.

Themes

Zeros from interference

For A decaying to tops, Djouadi et al. find Im κ=-1 exactly and |κ|≈1.5–1.7. An A carrying half the excess would shift the toponium peak by 10–70%. Cesarotti et al. arXiv:2611.27681 make the general case: in strongly coupled UV completions, destructive interference can put an amplitude zero parametrically below the heavy threshold. Absorptive effects turn that zero into a dip, and its position, depth and curvature constrain the UV. The two papers appeared independently on the same day.

Agents, where the answer can be checked

Petit Rosas et al. arXiv:2611.26688 had Claude Opus 5.5 work autonomously for days. It produced ε-pole-free bases for a two-loop five-point family with 18 elliptic sectors and an ε-factorized basis for a radiative-jet-function superfamily with a K3 sector. The authors pick the task because the output is verifiable, which is the standard Alimena argued for on 11-19. That contrasts with last week’s Codex reproduction of CMS J/ψ cross sections, which carried a 21% RMS spread. Bonnet-Guerrini et al. arXiv:2611.27079 find a jet foundation model whose classification flips when one soft neutral particle is added. They trace the infrared-safety failure to mixed reconstruction thresholds in pretraining. They then repair it either by removing three sparse-autoencoder directions or by letting an agent edit the weights directly in 50 queries.

Heavy-hadron rules under strain

Di Wang et al. arXiv:2611.27716 find that the KPW+SU(3)_F prediction for Ξ_c⁰→pK⁻ overshoots the measured rate by 17±6×, a 6.3σ discrepancy in a joint fit. Shirui Zhao et al. arXiv:2611.27363 predict D_s1(2460) radiative ratio 0.57, below Belle’s 0.74±0.08 from 11-17. They read the state as a ¹P_1/³P_1 mixture with a possible tetraquark component. Jiaxing Zhao et al. arXiv:2611.27014 fit bottomonium and lattice Ω_bbb jointly, and the fit favours Y-shaped over Δ-shaped confinement.

Lepton-collider generators

König et al. arXiv:2611.26718 build MiNNLO for lepton collisions and apply it to dijets in Powheg. Dave et al. arXiv:2611.27883 match YFS soft-photon resummation to NLO for radiative-return μμ/ππ. They agree with BabaYaga at the per-mille level but differ from KKMC by up to 2%, which matters for HVP inputs.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.27704 (Djouadi et al.): Required reading before anyone fits the threshold excess with a scalar component again.
  • arXiv:2611.26688 (Petit Rosas et al.): The first agent paper here where the agent produced new results rather than reproducing old ones.
  • arXiv:2611.27716 (Wang et al.): Lists eight Λ_c modes that would decide whether KPW survives. Experimentalists can act on that list directly.
  • arXiv:2611.27985 (Barenboim et al.): Asymmetric matter gives ν_μ survival a genuine sinδ T-odd term, and the usual “no T violation in disappearance” test is an identity. This is relevant because ν_μ disappearance anchors the mass-ordering fits dissected on 11-11 and 11-17.
  • arXiv:2611.26718 (König et al.): The first complete NNLO+PS event generator for lepton collisions.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.27611 Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges — Shuntaro Aoki et al. (hep-th). A second analytic triple-exchange bispectrum in a week, now with unequal masses.
  • arXiv:2611.27265 Features investigated… — Steen Hannestad et al. (astro-ph.CO). A Δχ² = 10 monodromy feature disappears once ACT/SPT data are added; A_osc<0.056.
  • arXiv:2611.26691 The cosmological lithium problem and how decaying relics still solve it — Maksym Ovchynnikov (hep-ph). Few-hour relics decaying to ~100 MeV ν̅_e survive the current D, ⁴He and N_eff bounds.
  • arXiv:2611.27456 Flavor-Modulated Neutrino Communication… — Bipin Singh Koranga et al. (hep-ph). Through-Earth neutrino messaging reaches 1.4×10⁻⁴ bit/s at best.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.27704 — A pseudoscalar Higgs boson interfering with toponium: a QCD analysis of gg→A→tt̅ near threshold (Abdelhak Djouadi et al.)

Djouadi and Ellis show that an A near 2m_t must interfere with η_t, and that its line shape is a Fano profile fixed by one complex number κ. Both live in the colour-singlet ¹S_0 channel and share the same Coulomb Green function. If A decays only to tt̅, unitarity forces Im κ=-1 exactly and independently of g_Att. The narrow-width rate then changes by δ=-2/|κ|², with an exact amplitude zero at ϵ=-Re κ. Coulomb resummation enhances Γ_A by 1.2–3.5×, which gives resummed κ≈-1.14 to -1.37 minus i, so |κ|≈1.5–1.7: maximal distortion. The zero then sits at ϵ≈1.1–1.4, and the ¹S_0 rate drops 70–90% relative to signal alone.

Because toponium lies below M_A, where Re κ<0, the interference there is constructive. For f=50%, the η_t peak rises by 1.69, 1.19 and 1.12 at M_A=350, 365 and 380 GeV. The threshold excess over toponium is 0.95, 1.22 and 1.45 coherently, versus 1.57, 1.44 and 1.41 incoherently. An A at 350 GeV carrying half the excess is thus essentially invisible. At 20% m_tt̅ resolution, toponium and toponium+A differ mainly in normalization.

Caveats are stated plainly: - The hard process is LO without K-factors. - The Coulomb potential is LO with a constant Γ_t. - The matching to fixed order is an interpolation. - Top decays and spin correlations are not simulated.

Peak enhancements still move by up to ~20% under these variations. The paper also retracts the robustness of its own earlier wide-window probe, which shifts from ≈4 to ≈3, or ≈6 with a frozen form factor.

arXiv:2611.26688 — Agent-guided construction of Feynman integral bases (Pau Petit Rosas et al.)

Claude Opus 5.5, driven by two “skills” (roughly 4,500 lines of instructions and 15k lines of mostly Mathematica code), produced bases for two families. For each, the authors state that no such basis existed before. Every candidate passes a deterministic gate before acceptance: an exact-in-ε IBP reduction on a kinematic slice, an honesty check, and an invertibility check. An agent error can therefore waste CPU time but cannot enter an accepted basis.

Two-loop five-point QED pentabox with m_e,m_μ (seven scales, 232 masters): - Classification. The agent classified 80 sectors as canonical and 18 as elliptic. Five of the canonical sectors need nested roots. - Pole removal. It started from 23,254 entries with 1/(a+bε) poles. After ~155 accepted master changes over eight days, the census of offending entries was empty. - Result. The final system is pole-free and at most quadratic in ε. Its diagonal blocks are ε-factorized in all 75 non-nested canonical sectors.

Radiative-jet-function superfamily (124 masters): - K3 sector. On a second pass, the agent identified a K3 sector, which the authors confirmed. - ε-factorized form. It then reached full ε-factorized form in ~4 days with no dedicated skill. That change of basis uses 8 elliptic periods, 3 K3 periods and 108 DE-defined functions.

Total list-price costs were ~$1.8k and ~$1.0k.

Caveats: - The five-point DE exists only on slices; its full kinematic reconstruction is outstanding. - Neither basis is optimized for evaluation. - Humans intervened once substantively: the agent wrongly concluded two blocks couldn’t be factorized because it held higher-sector bases fixed.

arXiv:2611.27716 — Challenging the Körner–Pati–Woo Theorem in Charmed Baryon Decays (Di Wang et al.)

KPW+SU(3)_F links Λ_c⁺→Ξ⁰K⁺ to Ξ_c⁰→pK⁻. Using BESIII partial waves, the relation predicts ℬ(Ξ_c⁰→pK⁻⁾ at 17.2±6.0 times LHCb’s measured value. A five-observable joint fit gives χ²_min=45.2 for 2 dof, a 6.3σ discrepancy. The fit has to drag ℬ(Λ_c⁺→Ξ⁰K⁺⁾ from 5.5 to 1.38×10⁻³, a 5.9σ pull.

Rescuing KPW requires large SU(3)_F breaking: - pK⁻ channel: S/P-wave magnitude shifts of at least 76% and relative phases of at least 17.8°. - Decuplet sector: predicted α(Λ_c⁺→Δ⁺⁺K⁻⁾∈[-0.91,-0.83] against a measured +0.55±0.04, a 16–20σ sign flip. Fixing it needs a P–D phase shift of at least 93.5°.

The theoretical argument is qualitative. Colour-sextet diquarks embedded in larger singlets, via gluons or baryon–meson colour space, evade the valence-colour projection.

Caveats: - BESIII also allows an S-wave-dominated Ξ⁰K⁺ solution. - Branching fractions alone give a wider ratio range, [5.6±1.5, 18.7±5.0]. - The companion Σ⁺K⁻ test depends on the disputed Ξ_c⁰→Ξ⁻π⁺ normalization.

The actionable output is a set of isospin-only KPW relations, where breaking is expected at ~1%. These cover eight Λ_c⁺ modes and include the requirement Δ⁺η⁽’)=0. One already looks strained: the predicted ℬ(Δ⁺K_S⁰⁾⁼⁽².99±0.13)×10⁻³ sits above BESIII’s <2.54×10⁻³.

Full text for the Barenboim et al. (arXiv:2611.27985) and König et al. (arXiv:2611.26718) picks was not supplied, so no deep dive is given for them.

item.title: Friday, November 20, 2026
item.description:
YR4 retired, γ tightened

Two numbers people quote by default were replaced today.

  • Higgs cross sections. The LHC Higgs Working Group’s Report 5 inclusive cross sections (Hayes et al. arXiv:2611.26281) supersede YR4. Central values are unchanged within the old errors, and most uncertainties shrink. PDFs are now the leading uncertainty for the best-predicted modes. With no N³LO PDF set available, the gluon-fusion PDF-order mismatch uncertainty is doubled relative to YR4. ATLAS’s Run 2 combination had already become theory-limited, and this is where that limit now sits.
  • CKM γ. LHCb’s new combination (arXiv:2611.26449) gives γ = 63.2°⁺²·³₋₂.₂ and the most precise charm-mixing parameters to date. It includes the first γ measurement from 2024 data.

The rest of the day: a resummation ambiguity that dwarfs last week’s GW worries, and a third independent hit on superradiance.

Themes

GW forecasts: the weak link moves upstream

Last week the nucleation rate held up (~8% from one loop), and the blame for unreliable forecasts shifted to wall hydrodynamics. Today the effective potential itself is in question.

  • Zhao et al. arXiv:2611.26417 compare thermal resummation prescriptions in 2HDMs. Partial dressing and Arnold–Espinosa differ by up to nine orders of magnitude in GW peak amplitude, and partial dressing has its own path ambiguity worth a factor ~3.
  • Qiu et al. arXiv:2611.26303 propose an improved partial dressing scheme that removes that scheme’s overlapping-momentum divergences.
  • Guo et al. arXiv:2611.25581 find an extra q⁻² high-frequency tail when the sound-wave source is dissipative.

Superradiance, third mechanism-level hit

Bošković et al. arXiv:2611.26541 find that self-gravity depletes superradiant clouds by orders of magnitude. It dominates over self-interactions above f_a≳6×10¹⁶ GeV(α/0.1), essentially the crossover Foster et al. found on 11-17. Bottaro (11-19) reached a similar conclusion via self-interactions. One new wrinkle: a binary companion can partly offset the depletion, so environment now enters the black-hole spin bounds on axions.

LZ, photon-mediated

Wang et al. arXiv:2611.25931 (ALP→dark photon) and Yin et al. arXiv:2611.26274 (axino→bino) post near-identical templates. Both use endothermic photon exchange, a three-bin Poisson fit, and halo plus boosted benchmarks, with halo fits at ~1.2 TeV/346 keV and ~506 GeV/326 keV. Neither abstract mentions solar capture, the constraint every LZ model since Pospelov has been judged against.

Measured νe cross sections

  • SBND. Aliaga-Soplin et al. arXiv:2611.25098 report the highest-statistics inclusive νe CC cross section on argon: 3.90±0.18±0.41×10⁻³⁹ cm². The data prefer generators that predict lower cross sections.
  • MINERvA surrogate. Dey et al. arXiv:2611.26271 release a surrogate MINERvA detector response that reproduces held-out 2p2h events.

Both feed the percent-level interaction-modeling target that Machado’s mass-ordering analysis set on 11-11.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.26281 (Hayes et al.): The new citation for every Higgs signal strength. Read the process-by-process N³LO–PDF mismatch treatment.
  • arXiv:2611.26449 (LHCb): A joint γ/charm-mixing fit, plus A_CP(KK) and A_CP(ππ) under different theory assumptions. That bears on charm CPV, where the SM still falls short. The abstract gives no asymmetry values.
  • arXiv:2611.26417 (Zhao et al.): Puts a number on how much resummation choice alone moves a GW forecast. Expect it to be quoted against any LISA projection.
  • arXiv:2611.26026 (Hager et al.): Super-leading logs at lepton colliders, arising from Glauber exchange off photon splittings. The authors conjecture that soft–collinear factorization fails even in pure QED, which is relevant to every FCC-ee non-global observable.
  • arXiv:2611.26541 (Bošković et al.): A short, independent confirmation that free-field cloud models are never realized.

From the community

  • arXiv:2611.25060 The BSM Rollercoaster, 1980-2000 — Savas Dimopoulos (hep-ph). A first-person account of why naturalness felt compelling, and how the landscape led to Split SUSY.
  • arXiv:2611.25806 Particle physics science communication with grass-roots Instagram: a success story — Freya Blekman et al. (physics.soc-ph). A crowd-sourced CMS@DESY account: 140k+ accounts reached in six months, with practical notes for other groups.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.26324 Zbb̅ couplings at the Large Hadron Collider — Radovan Dermisek et al. (hep-ph). Uses contact terms to show ATLAS Zh already excludes opposite-sign Zbb̅ at >9.5σ, and argues this route can eventually probe the LEP-era anomaly.
  • arXiv:2611.25943 Equation of state of hot and dense QCD at the physical point via the complex Langevin equation — Michael Mandl et al. (hep-lat). First continuum-extrapolated 2+1+1 results at large μ_B.
  • arXiv:2611.26291 Who Moved My Z Boson?… — Kevin Alberto Urquía Calderón et al. (hep-ph). Mechanistic interpretability finds an internal “Z feature” in a generative model trained on real LHC data. Steering it shifts the Z mass; removing it broadens the peak.
  • arXiv:2611.26125 NNLO QCD corrections to radiative and hadronic Υ(1S) decays — Xiangyu Chang et al. (hep-ph). The window ratio gives α_s(M_Z)=0.12135⁺⁰.0039_-0.0036.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.26281 — Predictions for Inclusive Production Cross Sections of the Higgs Boson at the LHC and HL-LHC (Robin Hayes et al.)

At 13 TeV and m_H=125 GeV, the R5 gluon-fusion cross section is 48.04 pb, 1.11% below YR4’s 48.58 pb. The uncertainty budget is reshuffled:

  • Shrank: δ(theory) goes from ⁺³.41_-5.57% to ⁺¹.63_-4.67%. The truncation and 1/m_t terms disappear because exact N³LO HTL and NNLO top and top–bottom mass effects are now included. δ(t,b,c) falls from 0.83% to 0.34%, and PDF+α_s goes from ±3.2% to ⁺².69_-2.28%.
  • Doubled: δ(PDF-TH) goes from 1.16% to 2.31%. The reason is concrete. Swapping PDF4LHC21 for the MSHT20×NNPDF40 aN³LO combination lowers σ(ggF) by about 4.7% at 13 TeV. MSHT and NNPDF aN³LO themselves disagree by about 3%, so the direct NNLO→aN³LO difference cannot be trusted as the estimate.

Conversion tables to aN³LO are supplied. QED DGLAP evolution is included for ggF (−0.74% at 13.6 TeV). An N⁴LO soft-virtual cross-check shifts the result by only −0.1%.

For VBF the two aN³LO fits agree, which makes the genuine order effect (+2.2%) meaningful. It is still left out of the central value. Users wanting a conservative band can add ±2.2% in quadrature, which takes the total from ⁺².5_-2.4% to about ±3.3%.

Why it matters: this is now the normalisation for every signal strength. For the best-predicted modes the limiting factor is a community decision on N³LO PDFs, not a missing calculation.

Caveats: - The ggF scale band widened, not narrowed. This follows from switching to an on-shell m_t and a 3-point scale variation. - The photon/QED treatment is admittedly not uniform across production modes.

arXiv:2611.26449 — Progress in measurements of the CKM angle γ and charm mixing at LHCb (LHCb collaboration et al.)

The joint beauty–charm fit gives:

  • γ=(63.2⁺².3_-2.2)^∘, versus (65.4⁺³.8_-4.2)^∘ in LHCb’s 2021 combination.
  • x_12=(4.2⁺⁰.4_-0.5)×10⁻³ and y_12=(6.18⁺⁰.17_-0.18)×10⁻³.
  • ϕ_2^M=(4⁺¹¹_-10) mrad and ϕ_2^Γ=(19⁺²³_-24) mrad.

Two technical points stand out. First, the B→Dh inputs constrain δ_D^Kπ well enough to sharpen y_12. Second, ignoring charm mixing would bias γ by roughly the current precision, so the fit must be simultaneous. The first Run 3 input (B⁻→Dh⁻, D→K_S⁰h⁺h⁻, 2024 only, 5.8 fb⁻¹) already reaches 6.7° by itself.

Why it matters: - The direct γ precision now approaches the indirect fits, quoted as 66.2⁺⁰.8_-3.2° (frequentist) and 65.7±1.3° (Bayesian). The central value sits about 2.5° below the Bayesian number. - The mixing phases reach the ~10 mrad level, against theory estimates of 1–5 mrad. CPV in mixing is still unseen. - A_CP(KK) and A_CP(ππ) are now fitted internally rather than treated as external inputs. The text supplied here stops before their values. The paper flags that the U-spin relation a^d_KK/a^d_ππ=-1, even with branching-fraction corrections, is fragile if the strong phases are small.

Caveats: - The baseline assumes universality of the mixing phases, which would fail if δ_h⁺h⁻∼10, and neglects CPV in CF and DCS decays. - The Run 1–2 γ inputs were not reinterpreted with the updated BESIII strong-phase inputs. - Correlations are only partially included.

arXiv:2611.26417 — Thermal Resummation Effects on Electroweak Phase Transitions and Gravitational Waves in Conformal and Non-Conformal 2HDMs (Yu-Bo Zhao et al.)

The authors apply multi-field partial dressing (PD, full thermal functions, scalar gap equations with field-dependent mixing), Parwani, and Arnold–Espinosa to identical zero-temperature 2HDM points. Any difference is therefore purely the resummation choice.

Conformal 2HDM: - PD yields α=𝒪(1) and T_p/T_c≃0.5, while the truncated schemes give T_p/T_c≳0.8. - Wherever all three complete, peak amplitudes order as PD > Parwani > AE. - The authors’ own earlier conclusion of limited conformal supercooling turns out to be an artefact of the truncated schemes.

Non-conformal 2HDM: there is no universal ordering. Over extended regions the prescription even decides between a first-order transition, a second-order transition, and symmetry non-restoration.

Headline numbers: on benchmarks, PD and AE differ by up to about nine orders of magnitude in peak Ω_GW and about 50× in peak frequency.

Formal result: the dressed PD tadpole has nonzero curl (Eq. 14), contradicting the path-independence argument of Bahl et al. Changing the integration contour shifts transition temperatures by up to 7% and the GW amplitude by up to about 3×. A follow-up traces the curl to the zero-momentum sunset in the gap equation.

Why it matters: last week the blame for unreliable forecasts moved downstream to wall hydrodynamics. This moves it back upstream to the effective potential, and the spread here dwarfs both.

Caveats: - The PD used is minimal: no sunset combinatorial factors and no lollipops, and their size is untested across the scan. - Gauge bosons get only Parwani-type Debye masses. - Tunnelling is restricted to the SM-like direction, checked at a single benchmark. - The Hubble rate ignores vacuum energy at the most supercooled points. - A non-runaway energy budget is assumed.

item.title: Thursday, November 19, 2026
item.description:
ATLAS limits look too well-behaved

Şahin et al. arXiv:2611.24065 read about 400 exclusion plots from 2020–25 ATLAS and CMS searches straight from the vector graphics.

  • CMS matches the nominal coverage: 66.1% of observed limits fall inside the 1σ band and 95.3% inside 2σ.
  • ATLAS puts 99.2±0.4% inside its 2σ band, which is too many.

Their pseudo-experiments allow three explanations: conservative uncertainties, low-count searches, or expected limits computed after a fit to data. The last is the default in common statistical tools, and the plots don’t say which method was used. This matters for the list of unclosed LHC excesses, which grew by a 3.5σ instanton-like entry yesterday.

The day’s boldest claim, Keshet’s 70/74.5 GeV WIMP line triads in 23,000 stacked clusters arXiv:2611.21595, shows why the method question matters. The blind scan alone gives 2.8σ trial-corrected. The quoted 6.1σ appears only after combining with the author’s own earlier samples.

Themes

Priors decide the GW verdict

Bringmann et al. arXiv:2611.23371 replace the power-law SMBHB background with a realistic population model. The PTA preference for a phase transition then drops from 2.8σ to 1.5σ. AbdusSalam et al. arXiv:2611.24625 find that LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA phase-transition constraints from O1–O4a depend strongly on the prior. Last week’s GW papers worried that predicted transition signals depend on poorly known hydrodynamics. These two show the same fragility on the data side.

Superradiance clouds, smaller again

Bottaro et al. arXiv:2611.23384 show that self-interactions let the 211 cloud feed the ground state faster than that state falls into the black hole. This caps the cloud mass, and below about 4×10⁶ M☉ the cap is lower than assumed. That is the same conclusion as Foster’s 11-17 gravitational Auger effect, reached by a different mechanism: black-hole spin bounds on axions need rechecking. On the lab side, Benabou et al. arXiv:2611.23374 cost-optimize detectors for the GUT-scale QCD axion. A 6 T toroid about 14 m across (~120 MCHF) beats the 16 T DMRadio-GUT design at roughly half its cost.

V_ud: the three-body piece

Chambers-Wall et al. arXiv:2611.24825 compute three-nucleon δ_NS matrix elements with quantum Monte Carlo. The 𝒪(α²⁾ terms are large enough to move V_ud at the 10⁻⁴ level. They also extract V_ud from ¹⁰C, the transition where Novario’s coupled-cluster calculation (11-17) came in 30% below QMC. The abstract gives no value, so the comparison has to wait for the paper.

Spectroscopy, with brakes on

Peng et al. arXiv:2611.24372 reproduce the K_SK_Sη’ dip and the 2.4 GeV enhancement through interference among known pseudoscalars, without BESIII’s extra X(2800). That undercuts the glueball reading of X(2370), as did Kang’s 11-10 sum-rule result that the X(2370) band can be empty. Danilkin et al. arXiv:2611.24694 extract the f₂(1270) and f₂′(1525) poles from radiative J/ψ multipoles without PDG input.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.24065 (Şahin et al.): Concrete evidence about how expected limits are being produced. Its recommendation, that publications state how expected limits are computed, is cheap to adopt.
  • arXiv:2611.24270 (ATLAS): The first published unbinned, fully differential collider cross section, Z+jets via OmniFold. It is released as particle-level events with unfolded weights, so anyone can construct new observables after publication.
  • arXiv:2611.23371 (Bringmann et al.): A public surrogate, binaryfog, that profiles over SMBHB astrophysics. If binaries take more than about 6.5 Gyr to merge, the phase-transition preference rises back above 3σ.
  • arXiv:2611.23384 (Bottaro et al.): An explicit cap on the 211 cloud mass, scaling as f_a², that reaches into stellar-mass spin bounds.
  • arXiv:2611.24671 (Agrawal et al.): An SU(12) unification that does not pass through SU(5). It predicts sin²θ_W = 1/2 at the GUT scale and E/N = 2/3, and comes with a bootstrap proof that new embeddings of this kind lie in the SU(8m+4) family.

From the community

  • arXiv:2611.23330 Training for sustainable scientific software in the AI era — Juliette Alimena (cs.SE). Argues that HEP software training should judge competence by the evidence behind a result, not by generated code. Timely, a day after yesterday’s Codex-agent reproduction of CMS J/ψ cross sections.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.23368 Steerability in top quark decays at the LHC — Tao Han et al. (hep-ph). Steerability is established at 7.7σ in boosted semileptonic tt̅. A cut at M_tt̅≲360–400 GeV isolates a steerable, singlet-dominated state, relevant to the toponium region.
  • arXiv:2611.23978 Geoneutrinos (and reactor neutrinos) do not visibly decay — Mauricio Bustamante (hep-ph). The first terrestrial limits on visible ν₁ decay.
  • arXiv:2611.24559 First observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed decay B⁺_c →J/ψD^∗+ — LHCb collaboration et al. (hep-ex). Observed at 5.4σ, with a ratio of 0.067±0.016 to the J/ψD_s⁺ normalization mode.
  • arXiv:2611.23983 Positron escape from dark matter spikes in black hole X-ray binaries — Mpho Kgoadi et al. (astro-ph.HE). Modeling the magnetic field near the horizon raises the cross section needed for the black-hole-spike explanation of the AMS-02 positron excess by 500–1400×.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.24065 — An Updated Meta-Analysis of LHC Exotic Physics Results (Ece \c{S}ahin et al.)

ATLAS expected-limit bands are miscalibrated, while CMS bands look fine. Şahin and Özcan extracted observed limits and ±1σ/±2σ bands directly from the SVG geometry of 168 ATLAS and 205 CMS exclusion plots. These come from 55 exotics publications (2020–25), with uncertainties from a bootstrap over publications. In normalized averaging, CMS sits at 66.1±4.4% (1σ) and 95.3±1.9% (2σ). ATLAS has 73.3±7.6% inside 1σ, compatible with nominal, and 99.2±0.4% inside 2σ, well above nominal. The raw-averaged ATLAS 1σ fraction is 81.8±5.9%, which is +2.3σ.

The 2σ excess survives several checks: - It persists in columns where the band edges are well separated (99.5±0.3%). - It holds in both publication-year halves and on a citation-independent subset. - The plot reading matches HEPData for 1522 of 1523 cross-checked points.

In the 2019 study, both experiments matched nominal coverage.

The pyhf toys separate the candidate explanations by which side of the band the observed limits avoid: - Low counts: with one expected event, 92% of limits land inside 1σ and none below. This mainly empties the lower side. - A-posteriori bands: reach about 99% inside 2σ only when the signal region itself constrains an uncertainty of half the background or more.

ATLAS has almost no points beyond either 2σ edge. The authors therefore favour bands that are too wide, from conservative uncertainties or a-posteriori computation, over low counts alone. Because most analyses fix backgrounds with control regions, they doubt a-posteriori bands explain the whole effect.

Caveats: - The scope is a topic-restricted exotics subset. - The authors cannot tell common practice from a few analyses. Single publications move ATLAS by up to about 1σ. - Özcan is an ATLAS author. - No paper in the sample states whether its bands are a priori or a posteriori.

The authors’ four-item disclosure list (tool and version, limit type, asymptotic vs. toys, convention) is the actionable output.

arXiv:2611.24270 — A fully differential charged-particle phase-space measurement of Z+jets production with ATLAS (ATLAS Collaboration)

ATLAS has published Z→μμ+jets (140 fb⁻¹, p_T^μμ>200 GeV) as an unbinned unfold of the full charged-particle final state. Each event averages about 50 tracks and exceeds 250 in some, so the unfold is effectively 150–750 dimensional. The release is particle-level MG5+Py8 events with OmniFold weights in fb, plus 162 weight variations (27 systematic, 135 bootstrap).

The method changes against the earlier 24-observable MultiFold analysis: - Particle Transformers replace the earlier MLPs. - Networks are pretrained on about 14M MG5+Py8-vs-Sherpa events. The authors call this essential because only about 247k data events pass selection. - Unfolding runs seven iterations. - Compute cost was roughly 400k A100-hours.

Showcase results: - Charged multiplicity: MG5+Py8 overshoots and Sherpa undershoots n_ch, by up to about 50%. - Energy correlator: the first all-charged-particle EEC in pp, at ≤5% precision, with clear perturbative, free-hadron and wide-angle regimes. Both generators miss the smallest-z region. - Jet shapes: C/A, k_t and anti-k_t jet shapes come from the same sample without recalibration. - Intrinsic dimension: the first measured jet intrinsic dimension, below 10 at all EMD scales.

Caveats: - Only charged particles are measured. - Hadron-species fractions and process labels are not constrained; they come from MG5+Py8. - The unfolding uncertainty is among the dominant terms and grows in low-statistics regions. - Users must validate each new observable on the released pseudodata, with at least 5000 effective events per bin. This is not a formality: finer n_ch binning drops to p=0.041, and m_j1 already sits at p=0.016. - No goodness-of-fit procedure is yet recommended for genuinely unbinned downstream use.

arXiv:2611.23371 — Seeing through the fog: astrophysical priors and the evidence for new physics in PTAs (Torsten Bringmann et al.)

binaryfog emulates holodeck SMBHB population spectra, including per-bin median, width and skew of the realisation scatter, in about 0.2 ms instead of about 3 min. That speed makes it feasible to profile over all six astrophysical parameters in new-physics fits to the 2026 re-run NANOGrav 15-yr CURN free spectrum.

Under NANOGrav’s own priors, replacing the (A,γ) power law with the population model lowers every new-physics preference:

Model Power law Population model
Phase transition 2.8σ 1.5σ
Cosmic superstrings 2.9σ 1.5σ
Inflation 2.8σ 1.5σ
Domain walls 2.1σ 0.7σ

The driver is that binary lifetime τ_f and inner hardening index can bend the binary spectrum at low frequency, which a power law cannot.

The result is prior-dominated: - Flat priors: 0.2σ. - Tomczak–Kormendy priors (the narrower widths of the underlying fits): 3.3σ, because those priors predict too faint a background. - Survey-average priors (the authors’ recommendation): 1.7σ. - HD+MP+DP+CURN spectrum: 0.6σ. - Lowering the spectrum by 0.1–0.2 dex, as pulsar red-noise priors may require: down to 1.0σ.

The binaries-alone fit pins τ_f near the 0.1 Gyr edge of its prior. Under survey-average priors, requiring τ_f > 2 Gyr pushes the phase-transition preference above 2σ, and τ_f > 6.5 Gyr pushes it above 3σ. The verdict is therefore tied to the final-parsec problem.

Caveats: - Significances are nominal. The χ² conversion ignores parameters that are non-identifiable under the null. - Orbits are assumed circular. - Frequency bins are treated as independent. - The per-realisation Gaussian likelihood is justified only in the three lowest bins. - The best-fit phase transitions sit at α≫1, beyond where the sound-wave template was simulated (α up to about 0.1). A strongly supercooled template gives 1.9σ, against 3.2σ with the power law.

item.title: Wednesday, November 18, 2026
item.description:
ATLAS sees instanton-like isotropy

ATLAS Collaboration arXiv:2611.22092 reports the first LHC search for QCD instanton-induced events, and it finds an excess of low-mass, isotropic events at 3.5σ. The data are 1.6 nb⁻¹ of very-low-luminosity 13 TeV collisions. The background is minimum-bias, predicted from data plus reweighted Monte Carlo, so soft-QCD modeling is where the scrutiny starts. The abstract doesn’t say whether the 3.5σ is local. The excess joins the 13.6 GeV diphoton and 146 GeV eμ on the list of unclosed LHC excesses, a list that has already prompted a look-elsewhere reckoning. The rest of the day: two more thermal LZ models, an ALP window closed with old LHC data, and several papers on what quoted errors mean.

Themes

LZ, thermal and composite

Buttazzo et al. arXiv:2611.21737 build inelastic dark matter from stable composite-Higgs resonances. Their mixed regime gives a few-TeV mass, ~300 keV splittings and ~10° mixing. The abstract claims consistency with solar capture and with the LZ high-energy sideband, the sideband search being one of the two decisive tests flagged in September.

Leng et al. arXiv:2611.22890 use a radion portal to land at 1 TeV with δ=340 keV. Their solar-neutrino check is only a proxy, with rates “comparable in magnitude” to IceCube’s reconstructed scales. That leaves the constraint every LZ model has designed around since September untested here, and Lin et al.’s 11-13 recomputation had just tightened it.

Windows closed, not loosened

  • The pion chimney. Blinov et al. arXiv:2611.21728 close the ALP mass window around the π⁰, which no search had covered, using the ATLAS monojet and inclusive-photon results. The key point is that mixing changes the two eigenstates’ lifetimes without equalizing them.
  • B→Ka. Banerjee et al. arXiv:2611.21764 add flavor-conserving ALP couplings, with the flavor change supplied by SM weak loops.
  • Neutrino dipoles. Fiorillo et al. arXiv:2611.21729 set μ_ν_e≲4.8×10⁻¹³μ_B from SN 1987A, superseding all existing bounds.

Last week’s audits mostly loosened limits; today’s go the other way.

What the error bars mean

  • HERA PDFs. Canonero et al. arXiv:2611.22891 treat quoted HERA systematics as themselves uncertain. That cuts χ² from 1363 to 1306 for 1131 dof, mostly at low x and Q², and widens the PDF uncertainties without shifting the central PDFs.
  • gg→ZH. Zhang et al. arXiv:2611.23020 find top-mass-scheme variations of 32–50% in boosted STXS bins, and show an inclusive K-factor cannot fix LO+PS samples.
  • Lensing H_0. Brady et al. arXiv:2611.21821 find the decreasing-H_0 trend with lens redshift drops to ~1σ once mass-sheet uncertainties are propagated.

This continues the week’s self-audit habit, now applied to inputs rather than to limits.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.22092 (ATLAS): A first search that comes back with 3.5σ. Read the minimum-bias background construction before reading the significance.
  • arXiv:2611.21728 (Blinov et al.): A clean kinematic argument that closes a window everyone had stepped around. It adds a separate bound from the π^±–π⁰ mass splitting.
  • arXiv:2611.21737 (Buttazzo et al.): The first LZ model in this run to check off solar capture, the sideband and gamma rays in a single abstract.
  • arXiv:2611.22891 (Canonero et al.): A substantial part of HERA’s notorious data–theory tension turns out to be error modeling, not physics.

From the community

  • arXiv:2611.22982 Muon Collider: Towards the Energy Frontier — Mark A. Palmer et al. (physics.acc-ph). A status review aimed at a mid-century facility. It lands alongside muon-collider projections for τ dipoles and leptophilic baryogenesis.
  • arXiv:2611.21997 Fundamental physics with quantum sensors in space — Jason Arakawa et al. (quant-ph). Aspen workshop proceedings making the mission case for clocks and atom interferometers.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.22421 Top-Quark Physics after Evidence for Toponium — Howard Baer et al. (hep-ph). Measured threshold cross sections span 3–13 pb. Part of that spread survives even between analyses using the same signal model.
  • arXiv:2611.23082 Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization. II… — Margherita Lembo et al. (astro-ph.CO). These are the strongest CPT-odd bounds to date. Planck PR4 EB gives a mild preference for a nonzero coefficient, which is relevant to the birefringence hint.
  • arXiv:2611.22723 AI-Assisted Analysis of CMS Open Data… — Zhipeng Cui et al. (hep-ex). A Codex agent under human review reproduces CMS J/ψ cross sections with mean ratio 1.000 but a 21% RMS spread.
  • arXiv:2611.21813 Probing τ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders — Dario Buttazzo et al. (hep-ph). At 10 TeV the projection is |d_τ|<6.6×10⁻²⁰ ecm, well beyond FCC-ee.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.22092 — Search for the low-mass isotropic signature of QCD instantons in pp collisions at √(s)=13 TeV using the ATLAS detector (ATLAS Collaboration)

The result. ATLAS fits an excess of soft, isotropic events in 1.6 nb⁻¹ of 2015 data at ⟨μ⟩=0.028. The observed significance is 3.5σ against an expected 1.5σ. The fitted signal strength is μ=2.3±0.6, corresponding to σ_vis=2.4±0.7 μb. The post-fit signal-region yields are ~3.9k signal on ~28.8k background, against 32,789 events observed.

The method. - Selection. Events are restricted to 10<S_T<20 GeV. Acceptance × efficiency is 7.4% for signal and 27% for background. - Classifier. An ABCDisCo DNN is trained on five track variables (AUCs 0.82 and 0.85). It defines a data-driven ABCD plane. - Non-closure correction. Residual correlations are corrected bin by bin using the mean of EPOS, Pythia 8 and Sherpa 3.

Caveats. As the digest warned, the background is the crux. - EPOS non-closure reaches 20% in the signal region before the fit. - The fit pulls the Sherpa 3 and EPOS-ABCD non-closure nuisance parameters by ~0.8σ. - The physics validation region sits systematically above the model. - Using an EPOS-only closure target gives μ=1.9±0.8 at 3.0σ. - The authors state plainly that “no background-only model can fully describe the data.” - The paper does not discuss look-elsewhere effects. - The theory cross-section varies by factors of ~20–24 under scale choices, so μ≠1 says little either way. - Control fits at 20–40 GeV in S_T return μ compatible with zero.

Why it matters. The text names what would distinguish an instanton from mismodeled soft QCD: the charm content predicted by the ‘t Hooft vertex, and the mass spectrum. Both remain unchecked.

arXiv:2611.21728 — Plugging the Pion Chimney (Nikita Blinov et al.)

The result. The authors diagonalize the a–π⁰ system exactly. At the chimney floor (c_GG/f=3×10⁻³ GeV⁻¹) the eigenstates are split by ~12.6 keV, far above the 8 eV π⁰ width. The two states share production but have different lifetimes, which leads to two complementary LHC constraints: - ATLAS monojet. The 10⁻³ GeV⁻¹ bound is rescaled by the survival probability to an effective radius of 12.5 m. This excludes everything except a window around m_π⁰, a few MeV wide at 3×10⁻³ GeV⁻¹ and 30 MeV wide at 3×10⁻². - ATLAS inclusive photon (139 fb⁻¹). In that window the boosted state decays early, and its two photons merge into a single isolated photon with a harder spectrum than the background. This closes the gap.

Together the two cover the chimney up to the EFT cap, c_GG/f≈0.15 GeV⁻¹ for Λ=1 TeV.

Above the cap. In KSVZ completions, colored states above ~1 TeV imply c_GG/f<1.4×10⁻³ (N·y_Q/2) GeV⁻¹, or at most ~10⁻² for the most generous allowed choices.

Other findings. - The K⁺-width bound disappears for m_a≈120–135 MeV, because an ALP passes KLOE’s π⁰ selection. - A purely kinematic bound from the π±–π⁰ splitting excludes 134.1–135.4 MeV. It lies entirely inside the photon exclusion.

Caveats. - The large-coupling region rests on a model-dependent UV argument; a DFSZ-type completion evades it. - The simulation is leading order with a single effective detector radius. - The authors could not reproduce stronger claims in arXiv:2609.21991.

Why it matters. The authors expect analogous chimneys near the η and η′.

arXiv:2611.21737 — Thermal Composite Dark Matter at LZ (Dario Buttazzo et al.)

The result. Stable fermionic resonances of the minimal composite Higgs model give three thermal inelastic fits to LZ230616 (E_R=248 keV in 2.84 t·yr): - (2,2)₀, composite Higgsino. It needs δ≳370 keV and M≳20 TeV (g_ψ≳3). The IceCube solar recast reaches ~20 TeV but misses the best-fit region. - Pure Y=0 triplet of (3,2)₁/₂. Strong dynamics alone supply a cross section suppressed by ξ²/16, which allows δ~150 keV at a few TeV. However, its recoil spectrum peaks low and disfavors a 248 keV event. H.E.S.S. line searches exclude M≲4 TeV and a narrow interval near 9 TeV. - Mixed triplets. A top-induced benchmark gives M~6 TeV, δ~300 keV and |θ|~10°. IceCube excludes masses below ~5 TeV.

The sideband argument. The sideband constraint is quantitative. At 5 TeV, |θ|=10° predicts N_HSB≈0.2, while 40° predicts N_HSB≈3.5. Larger mixing is therefore penalized by the empty sideband.

Caveats. - Sideband acceptance is taken as unity with no smearing, because the real acceptance isn’t public. - Results assume the SHM and negligible backgrounds. - Swapping the Vietze response for a Helm form factor shifts the required δ by 18–24 keV. - The relic calculations are deferred to an “in preparation” paper. - The 10° preference comes partly from a prior-dependent Bayesian posterior.

arXiv:2611.22891 — Canonero et al. (HERA PDFs) (Enzo Canonero et al.)

The full text of this paper was not included in today’s input, so no deep dive is possible. The digest records χ² falling from 1363 to 1306 (1131 dof) when HERA systematics are themselves treated as uncertain. In the digest’s summary, most of the improvement is at low x and Q², and PDF errors widen while central values hold. We’ll expand once the text is available.

item.title: Tuesday, November 17, 2026
item.description:
V_ud meets its contact terms

The most consequential posting is a pair from Novario et al. arXiv:2611.18830, arXiv:2611.18843. They give the first EFT evaluation of δ̅_NS across 12 superallowed transitions, using coupled-cluster calculations benchmarked against QMC.

  • Scale uncertainty: now negligible.
  • Three-body terms: some 𝒪(α²⁾ nuclear matrix elements matter, because they grow coherently as Z².
  • The floor: short-distance contact terms in the magnetic Gamow–Teller pieces. One combination fits from data. The other is strongly correlated with V_ud itself, which leaves δV_ud≃6×10⁻⁴.

The abstracts do not say where this leaves first-row unitarity, so the reader has to open the paper for the verdict. Elsewhere, nucleation theory turns out more robust than this week’s GW-forecast worries suggested, and the mass-ordering decomposition gets a general formalism.

Themes

Nucleation rates, checked from two sides

Zhou et al. arXiv:2611.18794 compute the thermal nucleation rate nonperturbatively on the lattice, using multicanonical HMC plus real-time Langevin, and take the continuum limit. The result differs from one loop by only ~8% in a 3D real scalar theory. Gil et al. arXiv:2611.20938 add higher-dimensional operators to the bounce consistently, prove field-redefinition invariance, and find modest corrections for moderately strong transitions. This week’s thread was that GW forecasts are hostage to transition dynamics. Today’s evidence suggests the rate is not the weak link; the ambiguity sits further downstream, in wall hydrodynamics (Barni, 11-16).

Mass ordering, as bookkeeping

Cerrone et al. arXiv:2611.21252 show that each experiment’s wrong-ordering Δm²_31 is a precision-weighted average over its bins. The weights depend on detector resolution, so each experiment reduces to one intercept, and how much two experiments help each other depends on how far apart their intercepts sit. This is the general machinery behind Machado’s 11-11 finding that the 1.9σ hint is a balance of opposing pulls. Cao et al. arXiv:2611.19416 give a cautionary companion: FRB+CMB ∑m_ν limits loosen to 0.3–0.4 eV once w_0w_a is allowed.

Charm hadrons, measured and computed

  • Strong phases: BESIII, presented by Zeng arXiv:2611.18944, updates strong-phase inputs for γ and charm mixing. The talk also reports the first observation of C-even DD̅ pairs above ψ(3770).
  • D_s1(2460) structure: Belle et al. arXiv:2611.20531 observe D_s1(2460)⁺→D_s^*+γ at >10σ, with a ratio to D_s⁺γ of 0.74±0.08 (stat. and syst. combined).
  • Lifetimes: Chia-Wei Liu arXiv:2611.20747 computes dimension-seven spectator terms at NLO. They make the published D⁺ width positive, giving τ(D⁺⁾⁼¹.41⁺∞_-0.76 ps. That upper error is not a typo.

Proofs and fits, audited

  • Lattice chiral fermions: Lu et al. arXiv:2611.20084 show the overlap Weyl fermion behind Lüscher’s construction is not reflection positive in 2D or 4D at finite spacing. That bears directly on the Witten/Hsu/Liu chiral-lattice thread from 11-05 and 11-13.
  • GUT no-go: Chen et al. arXiv:2611.20386 formalize a SUSY-GUT R-symmetry no-go in Lean 4, and find and close a gap in the published proof along the way.
  • Likelihood fits: Zhu et al. arXiv:2611.19355 are covered under Worth a look.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.18843 (Novario et al.): The long version of the V_ud result, with an explicit roadmap for which nuclear input would break the contact-term degeneracy.
  • arXiv:2611.21252 (Cerrone et al.): Extends the mass-ordering sum rule to atmospheric neutrinos in matter. For DeepCore, the intercept separation from JUNO is nearly independent of δ_CP and θ_23.
  • arXiv:2611.18833 (Foster et al.): A gravitational “Auger effect” drains the first superradiant level of the QCD axion after saturation. It can suppress continuous-GW signals, and the authors say existing spin-down limits need revising.
  • arXiv:2611.20356 (Ahmed et al.): Closed-form triple-exchange bispectrum. The Planck template overestimates the amplitude by up to 1.8× and biases the mass low.
  • arXiv:2611.19355 (Zhu et al.): Adaptive integrators can make the normalization jump discontinuously, producing artificially low NLLs. The motivating case is a CMS fully-charmed tetraquark search, and tighter tolerances alone don’t fix sharply localized terms.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.19498 K_1^(1870) and 3S-2D mixing in the strange meson sector* — Ting-Yan Li et al. (hep-ph). The first interpretation of BESIII’s 11-10 state. A 3S–2D mixture gets the mass and width right, but the authors flag that the predicted Kη’ mode is subordinate, which sits awkwardly with the channel the state was seen in.
  • arXiv:2611.20762 Muon and Tau Anomalies and Δα_had⁽⁵⁾⁽M_Z²⁾ in the Standard Model — Stephan Narison (hep-ph). A data-driven HVP review that still finds a 2.1–3.5σ g-2 window and questions the White Paper’s lattice averaging.
  • arXiv:2611.19831 Exploring X17 Couplings through Meson Dalitz Decays — Xuan Wang et al. (hep-ph). Pure-vector X17 couplings are in tension with charm Dalitz data, and axial |g^A_c,s|∼10⁻³ is needed.
  • arXiv:2611.21338 Generating a simple silicon detector simulation with an open-weight large language model — Charlie H R Bamber et al. (hep-ex). A local 27B model with MCP tools; 42% of runs match the reference simulation.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.18843 — Ab initio calculations of δ̅_NS and extraction of V_ud using effective field theory (Samuel Novario et al.)

The result is a nuclear-structure floor of δV_ud≃6×10⁻⁴, about twice the 3×10⁻⁴ quoted for the standard V_ud=0.97373(31). It comes from the second, unfitted combination of the contact LECs g^NN_V1,2 that renormalize the magnetic GT NMEs, which is strongly correlated with V_ud.

The main new input is coupled-cluster NMEs for all 12 transitions from ¹⁰C to ⁵⁴Co, computed with the 1.8/2.0 (EM) and NNLO_sat interactions. The CC uncertainty combines CCSDT-1 triples corrections with N_max 8→10 convergence. Several other ingredients feed the analysis: - Three-body Fermi NMEs: The Z²-enhanced 𝒪(α²⁾ terms come from a density approximation. It reaches |M⁺³b_F,p|∼200 for ⁵⁴Co and matches QMC (-18.6 vs. density estimates -17.7 to -20.3 for ¹⁴O). - Single-nucleon input: g_V(m_n)=1.01143(12), with the γW-box choice worth 7×10⁻⁵ in V_ud. - Corrections to earlier work: The authors restore a missing 𝐋^CM term and fix a sign error in the spin-orbit potential. Both changes are numerically non-negligible because of large cancellations.

Caveats: - For ¹⁰C, the CC M^mag_GT,p is 30% below QMC. The authors suspect clustering or Hamiltonian differences, and say this degrades the V_ud fit quality. - δ̅_C is still taken from the traditional evaluation rather than computed ab initio. - The extracted text ends before the fit section, so neither the central V_ud nor the first-row unitarity verdict could be checked here.

arXiv:2611.21252 — Mass ordering synergies and the role of the detector response (Vanessa Cerrone et al.)

The wrong-ordering solution of any experiment is an inverse-variance weighted average of per-bin preferred Δm²_31,IO. Every experiment then reduces to one intercept b=Δm²_31,IO+Δm²_31,NO, and pairwise synergy is (b_A-b_B)²/(σ_A²⁺σ_B²⁾. Intercepts below are in units of 10⁻⁶ eV².

Experiment Intercept b Main dependence
JUNO 25.7 at a_res=2.61% (data: 27) Moves ~10 between 2% and 4% resolution
Accelerators 103.8-11.6(cosδ_CP+cosδ^IO_CP) δ_CP
DeepCore (ν_μ disappearance, reference) 119.7 θ_23
ORCA6 ~11 below DeepCore Mostly from the shower sample

Above the MSW resonance the ν_μ frequency is δ_CP-independent, so the atmospheric intercept barely moves with δ_CP. As a result, JUNO+DeepCore (all channels) synergy is nearly fixed. JUNO+NOvA synergy, by contrast, varies by about 2× with the true δ_CP.

Caveats: - The analysis uses statistics only, with solar parameters and θ_13 fixed. - DeepCore is modeled on the 21,402-event golden sample. The 9.3-yr CNN sample lies above the computed band. - The NOvA–DeepCore estimates are lower bounds. - Published uncertainties cannot yet separate the accelerator and DeepCore bands.

arXiv:2611.18833 — Black Hole Superradiance and the Gravitational Auger Effect (Joshua W. Foster et al.)

Newtonian self-gravity mediates 211+211→322+BH transitions, with amplitude coefficient ℐ_G≃-0.0914. That is ~50× the quartic coefficient ℐ_λ≃+0.00184. The two have opposite signs because black-hole recoil cancels the uniform field and leaves only the tidal part.

Self-gravity dominates for f>f_×≃6.1×10¹⁶ GeV (α/0.1). That puts the QCD axion permanently in the moderate self-coupling regime: cancellation would need α≃0.6, beyond where 211 is superradiant.

The authors evolve a 33-level model for 10 M_⊙, χ_0=0.9, α_0=0.1: - 211 depletion: 211 drains to 10⁻³ of its peak within 10⁵ yr, versus 5×10⁸ yr without scattering. The two-level estimates are T_SG∼0.3 yr against T_GW∼4×10⁵ yr at α=0.1. - Continuous-GW lines at aLIGO design sensitivity: 211 drops from up to 10⁴ lines to <0.05. 322 drops from ~10³ to <0.1. - Spin-down: n44 overtones cap 322 at ≲10⁻⁴ of the BH mass. 322 spin-down therefore starts earlier but proceeds slower.

The spin-down nuance matters. The authors say the net effect on spin constraints is unclear and needs population studies. Only bounds using levels beyond 211 need revision; supermassive-BH 211-only limits are largely unaffected.

Caveats: the treatment is hydrogenic α≪1 with Newtonian self-gravity. It neglects self-energy level shifts and GW cross-annihilation, and the rates are unreliable for α_0>0.2–0.3.

item.title: Monday, November 16, 2026
item.description:
B→γℓν goes to three loops

Three groups posted pieces of an N³LO prediction for B⁻→γℓ⁻ν̅ on the same day. Two compute the photonic radiative jet function at three loops. Two obtain the three-loop Lange–Neubert kernel for the B-meson LCDA, one by direct calculation and one by a conformal bootstrap that needs no new three-loop diagrams. The practical payoff is a cleaner extraction of λ_B. This carries 11-13’s loop-count run from QED and V+jet into heavy-flavor SCET. Elsewhere: FCC-ee tomography joins the κ_λ question, bubble-wall hydrodynamics turns out to be non-unique, and dark-matter limits move in both directions.

Themes

Exclusive B at N³LO

Huang et al. arXiv:2611.18202 find that the largest three-loop effect comes from the jet function, not the recently computed hard correction. Liu et al. arXiv:2611.18206 compute both the kernel and the jet function using a regulator-free IR subtraction, which enables N³LL resummation. Ji et al. arXiv:2611.18204 bootstrap the kernel and verify RG invariance of the factorization formula. None of the abstracts reports a comparison of the overlapping results, so that is the first thing to look for.

Form factors: a sign and a |V_cb| input

Zhang et al. arXiv:2611.17800 find that the K⁺→π⁺ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ vector form factor is negative, V(0)<0. The significance is 5.8–7.9σ at a heavy charm mass, falling to 2.0–3.4σ after extrapolation to physical charm. Qu et al. arXiv:2611.17945 combine LCSR at large recoil with FNAL/MILC and HPQCD lattice data in BGL to extract |V_cb| and R(D). The abstract quotes neither number, so it’s unclear which side of September’s inclusive-vs-exclusive |V_cb| split it lands on.

Bubble walls without a unique profile

Barni et al. arXiv:2611.17402 arXiv:2611.17411 show that when the sound speeds on either side of the wall differ, (ξ_w,α_N) no longer determines a single stationary flow. A new “mixed hybrid” class appears, and its GW spectrum is mimicked by ordinary hybrids. Specifying the microphysics removes the ambiguity, and the public code HydróDex implements the full classification. This sharpens 11-13’s warning that a GW forecast is only as good as its transition dynamics. Formaggio et al. arXiv:2611.17401 add that a first-order QCD transition needs b≳0.028, which then has to be diluted by ~6.5 e-folds of little inflation.

Dark-matter bounds, in both directions

  • Supernova core heating. Suezaki et al. arXiv:2611.17922 count each DM particle once, which weakens the Fornax σ_νχ limit by ~50×. Applied to low-surface-brightness galaxies, the same method gives 8.5×10⁻²⁵ cm² at 1 GeV.
  • Supernova cooling. Cappiello et al. arXiv:2611.17604 show that resonant s-channel scattering on neutrinos can trap neutrinophilic DM and weaken or evade cooling bounds.
  • Superfluid helium. TESSERACT Collaboration et al. arXiv:2611.17365 measure >99% loss of the phonon signal into superfluid ⁴He, which rules out submerged sensors.

This is the week’s audit habit, now applied to limits.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.18202 (Huang et al.): The paper to open from the trio. It identifies where the three-loop weight sits and connects it directly to the λ_B extraction.
  • arXiv:2611.18136 (Altomonte et al.): Z density-matrix tomography in ZH at FCC-ee gives κ_λ to ±2.9 independent of the rate, close to the quantum-Fisher-information limit of about ±1. It reports magic in three measures, which partly answers Shen’s measure-dependence audit (11-09).
  • arXiv:2611.17402 (Barni et al.): The standard two-parameter description of bubble flows can be ambiguous, and dense matter is where that ambiguity is physically realized.
  • arXiv:2611.17800 (Zhang et al.): The first near-physical-pion lattice determination of the sign of V(0). Read the charm extrapolation before quoting the significance.
  • arXiv:2611.17416 (Tong): What a detector actually sees after monopole–fermion scattering. Hard tracks carry the standard quantum numbers, and a soft cloud of pairs carries the exotic ones.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.17651 ⁸B Solar Neutrino Measurements of Solar Core Size and Temperature… — Kamiokande Collaboration et al. (hep-ex). Combined with SNO, the core’s outer bound is 0.268 R_⊙ (B16+GS98). The quoted central temperature assumes nominal core density and size.
  • arXiv:2611.17422 The Full-Shape Analysis of the Fading Dark Sector Model — Georges Obied et al. (astro-ph.CO). The model is preferred over ΛCDM at 4.1σ and beats w_0w_a by Δχ²⁼⁻⁴ at equal parameter count.
  • arXiv:2611.17990 ESME stays positive: event generation with positive weights — Melissa van Beekveld (hep-ph). Positive-definite NLO+PS matching in PanScales, a structural fix for the negative weights that Frederix’s Born spreading (11-05) reduced.
  • arXiv:2611.18290 Are hybrid hydrodynamic models missing soft-pion physics? — Osvaldo Ferreira (ExTrEMe Collaboration) et al. (nucl-th). No parameter set fits ALICE’s low-p_T pions, while kaons and protons are fine.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.18202 — Next-to-Next-to-Next-to-Leading-Order Prediction for the Radiative B_u⁻→γℓ⁻ν̅_ℓ Decay (Yong-Kang Huang et al.)

What they did. The photonic radiative jet function J_γ is now known at three loops, which completes the leading-power N³LO ingredients for B⁻→γℓν̅. Two independent Feynman-gauge calculations agree: one from the SCET operator definition (1372 diagrams, 68 masters) and one from the hard-collinear region of full QCD. The masters were obtained both analytically and with AMFlow to 80 digits. A new photon-singlet colour structure, d^abcd^abc, appears with weight Q_Σ/Q_ext=1 for u,d,s,c. It is finite and independent of L.

At μ=1.5 GeV, the one-, two- and three-loop terms shift J_γ by −9.8%, −5.0% and −3.4%. The form factor at E_γ=2.2 GeV moves 0.340 → 0.318 → 0.300 from NLO+LL to N³LO+NNLL. Using Belle’s R_π, the extracted λ_B(1 GeV) goes 501 → 462 → 430 MeV. The new jet coefficient alone accounts for 449 → 430 MeV.

Why it matters. This supports the digest’s headline: the three-loop jet term, not the hard term, drives the latest shift in λ_B. All 27 logarithmic coefficients match the RG prediction built from the companion three-loop LN kernel (overlapping authors). No comparison with Liu et al.’s independent jet function appears in the text.

Caveats. - The perturbative series decreases slowly. - The three-loop jet effect depends on the LCDA shape at fixed λ_B: −4.2%, +2.5% and −5.8% for α=2.0, 1.7 and 2.5. - R_π and R_τ give λ_B values about 57 MeV apart. - The experimental input is weak: R_π=(1.7±1.4)×10⁻².

arXiv:2611.18136 — Quantum tomography of Higgsstrahlung: Higgs boson self-coupling and Z boson anomalous couplings (Clelia Altomonte et al.)

What they did. The three λ_hhh diagrams in e⁺e⁻→ZH are UV-finite as a set. They project onto only two structures: - a tree-level rescaling c(s), which sets the rate; - an effective CP-even coupling b_Z=κ_λβ(s), with β≈5.6×10⁻⁴ at 240 GeV, which changes the Z polarization.

Since the normalized Z density matrix is blind to c(s), tomography constrains κ_λ independently of the rate: - κ_λ: ±3.9, or ±2.9 with full angular information. The quantum-Fisher-information limit is about ±1, while the rate alone gives 28%. - Anomalous couplings (no assumptions): bounds at the 10⁻³ level, e.g. δ Re b_Z=1.1×10⁻³. - Rate-blind couplings: Im b_Z and Re b̃_Z are accessible only through the T̂-odd density-matrix entries.

Quantum observables. At 365 GeV and θ=π/2, the KCBS contextuality inequality is violated: 2.06 against the bound of 2. The inclusive state is neither contextual nor magic. The three magic measures disagree on where magic appears, and all are basis-dependent.

Caveats. - Signal versus SM background: the κ_λ-independent SM loops generate b̅≈-5.5×10⁻³, ten times the κ_λ piece. The per-unit-κ_λ Fano shifts (∼10⁻⁴) are comparable to the assumed 10% theory uncertainty on that background. - Hard ISR is deferred to reconstruction. - The quantum properties are insensitive to the anomalous couplings, shifting by at most a few ×10⁻³.

arXiv:2611.17402 — Microscopic Realizability of Non-unique Bubble Hydrodynamics (Giulio Barni et al.)

What they did. The setup is a constant-sound-speed equation of state with c_+>c_-, i.e. a stiff phase ahead of the wall and a softer one behind it. - New flows: “mixed hybrids” appear for c_-<ξ_w<c_+, with rarefactions on both sides of the wall. - Non-uniqueness: for larger hierarchies, the map from wall state to (ξ_w,α_N) folds. This happens only on the direct-hybrid, inverse-detonation and MH⁻ branches, and the direct-hybrid onset threshold is given analytically. - Benchmark (0.9,0.16): up to three profiles coexist at fixed (ξ_w,α_N), and inverse solutions reach α_N≃0.35. - Resolution: fixing the phase normalization Ψ_N plus an entropy-production ratio ℛ selects at most one profile.

Where the hierarchy can occur. - Thermal plasmas: c_+/c_-≃[43ln(m/T_+)]¹/2. Fold onset needs m/T_+≈70, and a ratio of 5 needs m/T_+∼10⁹. - SU(3) Yang–Mills: only superheated transitions place the softer phase behind the wall, giving c_+/c_-≲2.8, i.e. at most onset. - Finite density: μ_+γ_+=μ_-γ_-, so any hierarchy needs only μ_- near the mass threshold. Free nucleons at saturation give c_-≈0.16, the benchmark value.

Why it matters. It sharpens the digest’s point that GW forecasts inherit transition microphysics. For thermal early-universe plasmas the ambiguity is mostly academic; in neutron-star matter it may be real.

Caveats. - Sound speeds are taken as constant. - The finite-density case is treated only in the barotropic limit. - That Ψ_N separates competing profiles is verified only for the benchmark. - No lattice data exist for metastable phases.

item.title: Friday, November 13, 2026
item.description:
The LZ event, read elastically

Since September, almost every model of the 248 keV LZ recoil has used inelastic scattering, and each one has been built to survive solar capture. Bera et al. arXiv:2611.15957 drop the mass splitting entirely. Their dark matter is a Majorana fermion whose only electromagnetic interaction is an anapole moment, and the momentum dependence alone hardens the recoil spectrum enough to fit the event. The same coupling gives the relic abundance at ~300 GeV, and the model predicts more events at lower energies, which the full LZ run will test. The abstract checks collider and indirect-detection limits but doesn’t mention solar capture, which is where earlier readings of this event were excluded. Lin et al. arXiv:2611.16689 recompute solar capture itself, and Dai et al. arXiv:2611.16553 add a gauged B-L two-scalar model with a three-bin likelihood fit; the 11-03 Higgs-portal model gave rate estimates but no likelihood.

Themes

Loop counts go up

  • Li et al. arXiv:2611.15366 compute QED charge, mass and field renormalization analytically at six loops for arbitrary N_f, and say the methods open the way to six-loop QCD.
  • Gehrmann et al. arXiv:2611.15836 give full-color three-loop V+jet amplitudes, whose finite remainders live in a much smaller function space than the underlying integrals.
  • Two results aimed at lepton colliders: Haisch et al. arXiv:2611.15807 compute S and T at two loops in the Z_2 singlet model three independent ways, and Devoto et al. arXiv:2611.17171 supply two-loop mixed QCD–EW corrections to e⁺e⁻→bb̅.

This continues September’s precision-QCD run, now carried into electroweak observables.

Grover for haloscopes

Bogorad et al. arXiv:2611.14641 show that wavelike dark matter can act as a repeatable phase gate over many coherence times. A Grover search over N_bins frequency bins then gains a factor of √(N_bins). Bao et al. arXiv:2611.14629 work out a transmon version; reaching the QCD axion band takes 10⁶ entangled qubits. Soto Alcaraz et al. arXiv:2611.15878 use a two-node quantum network to tell an isotropic halo from a Gaia-like anisotropic one, which works only once Earth’s rotation sweeps the baseline across the sky. This adds a quantum-algorithm route to the haloscope readout work covered on 11-05.

Supercooling, with consistency checks

Zhang et al. arXiv:2611.14593 find that three different criteria for a transition completing share the same boundary. Close to that boundary, though, a homogeneous cosmology can’t be justified, so the claimed arbitrarily strong monopole suppression doesn’t hold up. Chaudhuri arXiv:2611.16845 finds a fast, strongly supercooled electroweak step in scale-invariant models. The LISA signal depends on the acoustic GW description still applying in that regime. Cassidy et al. arXiv:2611.15856 find that GW and di-Higgs predictions survive added dimension-six operators, but the Higgs trilinear does not. Same lesson as 11-03: a GW forecast is only as good as its transition dynamics.

Top SMEFT, two ways to slice

ATLAS arXiv:2611.16347 fits 33 Wilson coefficients across nine top-associated processes and sees no significant deviation. It also compares generic object-counting categories with process-targeted regions; the targeted regions give better sensitivity for most coefficients. Kumari et al. arXiv:2611.15274 make a parallel point about taggers. Taggers with similar AUC differ by up to 3× in discovery significance on CMS Open Data, and the particle transformers extend the Z’ mass reach by 400 GeV.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.15957: The first minimal elastic fit to the LZ event, with a relic-density coincidence and a falsifiable prediction at lower recoil energies.
  • arXiv:2611.16689: Solar capture, the constraint every LZ model has designed around since Pospelov, recomputed with a transport equation. When nuclear scattering is rare, captured DM never thermalizes and annihilation drops by orders of magnitude. For the inelastic higgsino, though, the bound on the splitting tightens by tens of keV.
  • arXiv:2611.16347: A template for multi-process SMEFT fits, with a direct head-to-head of categorization strategies.
  • arXiv:2611.14641: The cleanest argument yet that quantum algorithms can get around the coherence-time limit in dark-matter searches.
  • arXiv:2611.16544: Liu proves that Craig’s overlap measure and the Hsu/Witten continuum determinant agree for one SU(5) generation on T⁴, up to a local counterterm. This is the comparison Witten’s 11-05 note invited.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.16530 New measurement of BR(K⁺→π⁺νν̅) at the NA62 experiment — Silvia Martellotti on behalf of NA62 Collaboration et al. (hep-ex). The 2023–24 data double the sample. The abstract gives only the expected 5σ SM sensitivity, not the measured value.
  • arXiv:2611.15869 Discovering new physics with semitauonic b-hadron decays — Markus Prim et al. (hep-ph). A review arriving after Belle II’s September result eased the R(D^*) tension.
  • arXiv:2611.14616 N_eff, Radiative Dirac Neutrinos, and Flavor Physics from Leptoquarks — Patricio Escalona et al. (hep-ph). Fits the Belle II K⁺νν̅ excess, with N_eff bounds that can beat collider limits.
  • arXiv:2611.16715 Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth’s Mantle… — Michael Leyton et al. (physics.geo-ph). Across ~3 million fits, no mantle model reproduces the Kamioka–Jiangmen geo-neutrino gap. The authors conclude it is a local effect or statistical scatter.
  • arXiv:2611.16684 Is Spin Slow in Hot QCD? — Zi-Hao Liu et al. (hep-th). No: light-quark spin damps at the transport rate, which undercuts treating spin as a slow hydrodynamic variable.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.15957 — The Curious Case of Anapole Dark Matter at LZ: Minimal, Elastic and Testable (Sourav Bera et al.)

A Majorana fermion whose only electromagnetic coupling is a hypercharge anapole moment, a_χ χ̅γ^μγ⁵χ ∂^νB_μν, fits LZ230616 with purely elastic scattering. The interaction reduces to the NREFT operators 𝒪_8 and 𝒪_9. Their momentum dependence keeps the spectrum falling slowly at high recoil, which compensates for the halo-tail suppression. The fit is a binned Poisson likelihood over LZ’s public 2.84 t·yr data, with three S1c windows of 32 δ bins each. The background is fixed to LZ’s post-fit model, and the signal templates come from rescaling LZ’s ℒ_10 templates with NEST. Local significance from toys rises from 1.8σ at 100 GeV to 2.9σ at 300 GeV and saturates near 3.1σ above 500 GeV. The thermal-relic contour crosses the best-fit line at a_χ≃1.05×10⁻⁶ GeV⁻² and m_χ≃300 GeV, or 215–422 GeV within the 68% band. That point is allowed by an ATLAS 139 fb⁻¹ monojet recast and by white-dwarf heating limits.

Solar neutrinos are not computed here. The authors cite a celestial-probes study that included them and state that the white-dwarf limits are the most stringent in this mass range.

The prediction is sharp. At the full LZ exposure of 15.3 t·yr, the benchmarks reach 2.6–3.2σ (Asimov), mostly from the 250–500 phd window, which is nearly background-free and does not contain the observed event. XLZD would reach ≳9σ (11.7σ at 300 GeV).

Caveats: - Low predicted count where the event sits. At current exposure the model predicts only 0.064 events in the 500–600 phd window, against a background of 0.0097. - EFT validity. The EFT sits near its unitarity limit at LHC energies. - UV completions are strained. A tree-level vector completion needs ϵg_χ∼𝒪(1), which implies a strongly coupled dark sector. A loop completion needs charged states below about 100 GeV.

arXiv:2611.16689 — Dark matter evolution in stellar objects: A Boltzmann transport approach (Yen-Hsun Lin et al.)

The classical isothermal treatment of solar capture fails badly when nuclear scattering is rare. The method orbit-averages the Boltzmann equation into a master equation on an (E, L) grid of 192×48 cells. It evolves capture, orbit-to-orbit scattering, evaporation and s-wave annihilation together, and is valid because there are far fewer than one collision per orbit.

For SD scattering at 100 GeV and σ_χp=10⁻⁵⁰ cm², captured DM never thermalizes. Its central density ends up more than six orders of magnitude below the isothermal value, because freshly captured particles sit on wide orbits, often reaching beyond the solar surface. The classical treatment overestimates the annihilation rate by more than 2× below about 10⁻⁴⁶ cm² (SD) or 10⁻⁴⁹ cm² (SI). SD is suppressed much more than SI because hydrogen transfers energy poorly to heavy DM. The evaporation mass matches the classical value down to about 10⁻⁴⁷ cm² and falls below it at smaller cross sections. Orbit anisotropy inherited from the halo changes the annihilation rate by less than 4%.

For the inelastic Higgsino at 1.1 TeV, the result goes the other way. The full evolution confirms the equilibrium relation 2Γ_A ≃C_c.
